Lemma: H8486

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "South, the southern direction or region; also the south wind."
  Readable gloss: "Derived from the right-hand side as one faces east, this noun designates the south as a compass direction and geographic region. It appears frequently in the Tabernacle construction texts (Exodus 26-38) for the southern side of the structure, and in prophetic geography such as Isaiah 43:6 and Zechariah 6:6 for the southern quarter of the world. In two poetic passages, Psalm 78:26 and Song of Solomon 4:16, it specifically denotes the south wind. Spanish sur, French sud, and German Sueden uniformly reflect the directional sense."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "south, southward (direction/region)"
    Enriched: The cardinal direction south or the southern region, used as a locative or directional noun. Exodus 26:18 and 36:23 use it for the south side of the Tabernacle; Isaiah 43:6 pairs it with 'north' for geographic orientation. The he-locale form teymanah ('southward') accounts for most occurrences. Spanish al-sur, French de-sud, and German Sueden all confirm the directional reading.
    Existing Spanish translations: Temán, al-sur, desde-el-sur, el-sur, hacia-el-sur, hacia-sur, sur, sur., y-al-sur, y-desde-el-sur
  Sense 2: "south wind"
    Enriched: The south wind as a meteorological phenomenon. Psalm 78:26 describes God bringing forth the south wind by His power, and Song of Solomon 4:16 invokes it poetically: 'Awake, O south wind!' Spanish viento-del-sur and English south-wind in these two passages distinguish this from the directional sense.
    Existing Spanish translations: sur, viento-del-sur

}
